passages.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
passages.explain: God's love is the starting point. He gave His Son so that anyone who trusts Him can have life that lasts forever.
passages.whenToShare: Open with this when someone wonders whether God cares about them.

passages.text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
passages.explain: Everyone has fallen short of God's goodness, not just 'bad people'. It puts us all on the same level.
passages.whenToShare: Use gently when someone feels they're either too good or too bad for God.

passages.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
passages.explain: Sin earns death, but God offers eternal life as a free gift through Jesus.
passages.whenToShare: Show the contrast between what we earn and what God gives.

passages.text: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
passages.explain: Jesus didn't wait for us to clean up. He died for us while we were still far from God.
passages.whenToShare: Share when someone feels they need to sort their life out first.

passages.text: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
passages.explain: Responding to Jesus is simple: trust that He is Lord and that God raised Him from the dead.
passages.whenToShare: Use when someone is ready to respond and asks what to do.

passages.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
passages.explain: Salvation is a gift received by faith, not a reward for being good enough.
passages.whenToShare: Share with someone who thinks they must earn God's approval.

passages.text: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
passages.explain: Jesus doesn't claim to be one way among many. He says He is the way to the Father.
passages.whenToShare: Use with care and kindness when talking about other beliefs.

passages.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
passages.explain: When we're honest with God about our sin, He forgives and makes us clean.
passages.whenToShare: Share with someone carrying guilt or shame.

passages.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
passages.explain: In Jesus, a person gets a fresh start. The old life doesn't define them any more.
passages.whenToShare: Great to share right after someone says yes to Jesus.

passages.text: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
passages.explain: Jesus invites us into friendship with Him. He knocks; we open the door.
passages.whenToShare: Use when inviting someone to respond personally.

passages.text: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
passages.explain: The Gospel in one breath: Jesus died for our sins, was buried and rose again.
passages.whenToShare: A clear summary of the Gospel to share in any conversation.

passages.text: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep.
passages.explain: Paul points to hundreds of living witnesses who saw the risen Jesus.
passages.whenToShare: Use when someone asks whether the resurrection really happened.

passages.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
passages.explain: Jesus invites the tired and burdened to come to Him for rest.
passages.whenToShare: Share with someone who is worn out or struggling.

passages.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
passages.explain: Jesus came looking for people who are lost, not people who have it together.
passages.whenToShare: Use when someone feels too far gone.

passages.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
passages.explain: God can work even painful things for good in the lives of those who love Him.
passages.whenToShare: Share carefully with someone who is hurting, after listening first.

passages.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
passages.explain: God promises a future with no more death, grief or pain.
passages.whenToShare: Offer hope to someone grieving or angry about suffering.

passages.text: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
passages.explain: Jesus knows what it's like to be human. He understands our struggles from the inside.
passages.whenToShare: Share when someone feels God is distant from their pain.

passages.text: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
passages.explain: Written centuries before Jesus, this describes Him suffering in our place.
passages.whenToShare: Use when explaining why Jesus had to die.

passages.text: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
passages.explain: Jesus came for people who know they need help. The church is meant to be a hospital, not a museum.
passages.whenToShare: Share when someone says the church is full of hypocrites.

passages.text: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;
passages.explain: God saves us because of His mercy, not our good deeds.
passages.whenToShare: Share with someone who believes being a good person is enough.

passages.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:
passages.explain: Creation itself points to a Creator's power and nature.
passages.whenToShare: Use in conversations about science and whether God exists.

passages.text: The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
passages.explain: The universe displays God's glory and craftsmanship.
passages.whenToShare: Share with someone curious about science and wonder.

passages.text: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:
passages.explain: Everyone who receives Jesus becomes part of God's family.
passages.whenToShare: Share right after someone says yes to Jesus.

passages.text: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
passages.explain: Be ready to explain your hope, and do it gently and respectfully.
passages.whenToShare: A reminder for evangelists before every conversation.

passages.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
passages.explain: The Holy Spirit gives us power to be Jesus' witnesses everywhere.
passages.whenToShare: Encouragement for evangelists heading out.
